blog.headline: Why Your Old Low-Value Pages Are Dragging Down SEO Recovery
blog.angle: Google signals that legacy low-value content slows SEO recovery → Founders rush surface fixes hoping for quick wins → The real fix is ruthless, ongoing content pruning → Lesson: Your past content is your present liability.

linkedin.headline: Most SEO recoveries fail because founders can’t bear to delete their own dead weight.
linkedin.angle: Google’s warning on old low-value pages reveals that superficial SEO fixes won’t cut it; businesses must embrace ruthless content curation to truly recover search rankings.

facebook.headline: Think a few quick SEO tweaks will fix your rankings? Think again.
facebook.angle: Google says old low-value pages can hold back site recovery. Without cutting dead weight, how can your SEO bounce back? What’s your plan for ruthless content pruning?

instagram.headline: Your Past Content Is Your Present Liability
instagram.angle: Old, low-value pages don’t just sit quietly—they drag your SEO down long after you’ve tried to fix it.

threads.thread_hook: SEO recovery isn’t about polishing a few pages. It’s about facing the content you’re afraid to delete.
threads.angle: This thread breaks down why legacy low-value pages keep sites stuck in search limbo and how ruthless content curation is the only way forward.

stories.story_question: Can your SEO really recover without deleting old content?
stories.angle: Explores the tension between wanting quick SEO wins and the slow, necessary process of cutting legacy low-value pages to rebuild trust with Google.
